overview: Wipro is a Bangalore, India-headquartered global IT services, consulting, and business process outsourcing company, operating as a 20-F foreign private issuer with its fiscal year ending March 31. The company provides AI-powered IT services, consulting, digital transformation, infrastructure, cybersecurity, and engineering/R&D services to large enterprises across banking/financial services, consumer, technology & communications, health, and energy/manufacturing/resources verticals, with the vast majority of revenue (~99%) from IT Services and a small residual IT Products segment. Wipro operates through four Strategic Market Units (Americas 1, Americas 2, Europe, and APMEA) and trades on the NYSE as an ADR (1 ADS = 1 ordinary equity share) alongside its primary listing on Indian exchanges (BSE/NSE).

business_model.summary: Wipro generates revenue primarily from IT Services — time-and-materials and fixed-price/managed services contracts for application development & modernization, consulting, cloud, cybersecurity, data & analytics, infrastructure services, business process services, and engineering/R&D — billed mostly to large enterprise clients on multi-year master agreements. IT Products (hardware/software reselling, mainly in India) is a small, low-margin residual (~0.7% of FY2026 revenue). Revenue is largely recurring/contractual (managed services, annuity-style application support) blended with discretionary project-based transformation and consulting work, the latter being more cyclical and currently under pressure from delayed client decision-making.

revenue_streams.name: IT Services
revenue_streams.trend: stable-to-declining (USD IT services revenue -0.3% YoY in FY2026)

business_model.customer_type: B2B enterprise — large multinational corporations and government/public sector clients; top client ~4.6% of revenue, top 5 clients ~14.3%, top 10 clients ~23.7% (low concentration, diversified book)
business_model.geographic_mix: Americas (combined Americas 1 + Americas 2) ~62% of FY2026 revenue, Europe ~27%, APMEA ~11%; delivery heavily weighted to India-based talent with onsite/offshore blended delivery model; effective April 1, 2026 Latin America and Canada clients were realigned into the industry-sector-organized Americas 1/2 units

competitive_position.market_position: Wipro is the fourth-largest Indian IT services firm by revenue (~$10.8B FY2026 vs. TCS ~$29B, Infosys ~$19B, HCLTech ~$14B) and a mid-tier global player behind Accenture (~$64B). It has historically lagged its closest India-centric peers (TCS, Infosys) in organic growth and margin, following several years of leadership and strategy transitions (post-Capco/Rizing integration, CEO transition from Thierry Delaporte to Srini Pallia in April 2024).

moat_factors.description: Multi-year managed services and application support contracts embed Wipro into client IT operations, creating meaningful (though not insurmountable) switching friction, particularly in BFSI and legacy system support.

Large India-based delivery workforce (~230,000+ employees) provides a labor-cost advantage versus Western consultancies like Accenture/IBM, though this advantage is shared with TCS, Infosys, HCLTech, and Cognizant and is being compressed by AI-assisted coding reducing the economics of labor arbitrage.

Decades-long presence in global outsourcing and recognized as a 'Leader' by ISG, Everest Group, HFS Research, and Avasant across various service lines, but brand is weaker than TCS/Accenture/Infosys among large enterprise buyers.

Capco (acquired 2021) gives differentiated BFSI consulting capability; Rizing gives SAP/ERP depth; recently acquired Mindsprint (ex-Olam IT arm, closed mid-2026) adds food/agribusiness and consumer-packaged-goods vertical depth tied to a committed $800M, 8-year Olam contract.
Limited — IT services is a relationship/delivery business with few network effects versus platform or marketplace models.

weaknesses: Consistently slower revenue growth and lower operating margin than TCS and Infosys over the past several years
High dependence on commoditized application/infrastructure services vulnerable to AI-driven productivity gains compressing bill rates and contract values
Weaker brand pull in high-value consulting-led deals versus Accenture and in digital-native engagements versus smaller specialist firms
History of leadership churn (multiple CEOs/strategy resets over the past decade) creating execution inconsistency
Margin volatility — IT services operating margin fell to a 15-quarter low of ~16% in Q1 FY2027 on wage hikes and pre-growth investment, with management guiding only gradual recovery

growth_drivers: AI/GenAI-led repositioning: $1B AI investment (2023) with 200,000+ employees trained on GenAI principles, Microsoft Copilot partnership (AI360), and new 'AI Native Business & Platforms' unit pivoting toward a 'services-as-a-software' model
Large deal bookings accelerating sharply — FY2026 large-deal TCV of $7.8B (+45.4% YoY, 64 deals, four deals >$500M), providing revenue visibility even as organic growth remains subdued

M&A to build vertical depth and contract-anchored growth — closed acquisition of Mindsprint (Olam Group's IT arm, $375M, mid-2026) tied to an 8-year, >$1B TCV committed-spend Olam relationship ($800M committed), following earlier Capco (BFSI consulting) and Rizing (SAP/ERP) deals
Consulting-led go-to-market under CEO Srini Pallia emphasizing industry/functional consulting ahead of technology delivery to move up the value chain and defend pricing
Capital allocation discipline — large recurring buyback programs (₹150B/$1.6B buyback at ₹250/share completed in FY2026) supporting EPS and signaling confidence despite soft top-line growth

Potential cyclical recovery in discretionary technology/BFSI client spending as interest-rate and macro uncertainty eases, which would lift the currently depressed consulting/transformation revenue pool

business.risk: AI disruption of core delivery model
business.description: AI-assisted coding/development is estimated to reduce coding costs by roughly 25%, creating intense pricing pressure at contract renewal and risk of shrinking deal values and margin erosion across commoditized application development and maintenance work — the historical core of Wipro's (and peers') business model.

Transformation/consulting engagements are discretionary and have been delayed amid macro uncertainty; Q1 FY2027 management cited 'weak discretionary spending and delayed contract execution' as a continuing headwind, with IT services revenue guided to -1.5% to +0.5% sequential growth for Q2 FY2027.
Voluntary attrition running ~13.8-13.9% (TTM); competition for AI/digital-skilled talent is intense and shortfalls could delay execution or raise costs.

Overall concentration is low (top client ~4.6%, top 10 ~23.7% of revenue) but newer mega-deals (e.g., Olam's $800M committed spend) increase dependence on individual large relationships performing as contracted.

business.risk: Competitive intensity from peers and hyperscalers
business.description: TCS, Infosys, HCLTech, Accenture, and Cognizant all compete aggressively on price and AI capability; Wipro has historically grown slower than its closest peers, and TBR research expects it to continue lagging Infosys/TCS.

financial.description: Revenue is earned predominantly in USD/other foreign currencies but costs (largely wages) are INR-denominated; management estimates every 1% INR appreciation versus USD reduces reported INR revenue by roughly ₹200-250 crore per quarter, creating translation volatility in reported (and ADR) results.
IT services operating margin fell to a 15-quarter low (~16%) in Q1 FY2027 due to wage hikes and investment ahead of growth; CFO indicated recovery will take several quarters.

Large recurring buybacks (₹150B in FY2026) and dividends are capital-intensive; continued soft top-line growth could eventually pressure the pace of shareholder returns, though balance sheet remains net-cash and low-leverage.

regulatory.description: Evolving AI laws (e.g., EU AI Act) may impose governance, documentation, monitoring, and reporting requirements on Wipro's AI offerings, raising compliance costs and potentially limiting deployment speed.
Recent Mindsprint/Olam acquisition required antitrust clearances in multiple jurisdictions (Saudi Arabia, Australia), illustrating integration/approval risk inherent in Wipro's bolt-on M&A strategy.

As with all Indian IT services exporters, changes to US (and other developed-market) work-visa policy affecting onsite staffing economics are a structural regulatory risk to the offshore delivery model.
Expanding data localization and privacy regimes across client geographies raise compliance complexity for a company handling sensitive client data globally.

macro.description: IT services demand, particularly discretionary transformation spend, is closely tied to corporate capex and confidence; a global slowdown would likely further delay deal signings and extend the current soft-demand environment.
Higher-for-longer rates pressure client capex budgets (especially BFSI, Wipro's largest vertical at 34% of revenue) and can delay large transformation projects.
US-India trade and tariff dynamics, and broader US-China tensions affecting global supply chains, can indirectly affect client spending patterns and the attractiveness of India-centric delivery.

macro_factors.industry_outlook: Global IT services/outsourcing industry is navigating a structural inflection as GenAI tools compress the cost of application development and maintenance — the traditional labor-arbitrage core of the Indian IT services model — while simultaneously creating a new, uncertain revenue pool (AI advisory, agentic/AI-native development, platform engineering). Near-term discretionary spending remains soft across BFSI and technology/communications clients in major Western markets, though large-deal (annuity/managed-services) bookings across the sector have held up better than organic growth, suggesting clients are consolidating vendors and committing to longer-term relationships even as project-based discretionary work stays weak.
macro_factors.cyclicality: Moderate-to-high — consulting/transformation revenue is discretionary and cyclical with corporate capex; managed services/annuity revenue is comparatively stable and recurring, providing a partial offset.
macro_factors.interest_rate_sensitivity: Indirect but meaningful — client capex budgets (especially BFSI, the largest vertical) are sensitive to rate levels and macro confidence, which flows through to discretionary IT spending with a lag.
macro_factors.currency_exposure: High — revenue predominantly in USD/EUR/GBP and other client-market currencies, costs predominantly in INR; reported (and ADR, in further-converted USD) results are sensitive to INR appreciation/depreciation and cross-currency moves among client-billing currencies.
key_input_costs: Skilled IT labor wages (India and onshore)
Cloud/data-center and third-party AI model/platform costs

recent_developments.event: Q2 FY2027 results scheduled for October 15, 2026; guided IT services revenue of $2.574-$2.627B (-1.5% to +0.5% sequential constant currency)

Q1 FY2027 results: IT services revenue $2.61B (-1.4% QoQ); IT services operating margin fell to ~16%, a 15-quarter low, down 130bps QoQ/120bps YoY on wage hikes and pre-growth investment; net profit +0.6% YoY but -4.3% QoQ; large deal bookings $1.63B (+12.9% QoQ) across 13 deals; CEO cited weak discretionary spending and delayed contract execution

Completed ₹150B (~$1.6B) buyback at ₹250/share for up to 60 million shares (~5.7% of paid-up capital); promoter Azim Premji tendered ~23.3 million shares, with his effective stake nudging up to ~4.12% post-buyback (family/trust group holds ~21% combined)

Completed acquisition of Mindsprint (Olam Group's IT services arm, Singapore-based) for $375 million, anchored to an 8-year Olam Group IT services engagement expected to exceed $1B in TCV with $800M committed spend; adds food/agribusiness, manufacturing, retail/CPG and healthcare vertical depth

FY2026 full-year results: gross revenue ₹926.2B (+4.0% YoY); IT services revenue $10,478.1M (-0.3% YoY); IT services operating margin 17.2% (+20bps YoY); large-deal bookings $7.8B (+45.4% YoY, 64 deals, four >$500M TCV); total bookings $16.4B (+14.0% YoY); attrition 13.8% TTM; CEO Srini Pallia announced pivot to 'services-as-a-software' model via new AI Native Business & Platforms unit
Realigned Global Business Lines effective April 1, 2025, with Technology Services under Nagendra Bandaru to sharpen consulting-led, AI-powered, industry-specific focus
1:1 bonus equity/ADS issue completed (record date Dec 3, 2024); ADS-to-ordinary-share ratio unchanged at 1:1 post-bonus
Srinivas Pallia became CEO & Managing Director, succeeding Thierry Delaporte, marking a return to internally-promoted leadership after Delaporte's four-year external-hire tenure

items.notes: Implies -1.5% to +0.5% sequential growth in constant currency; follows a Q1 FY2027 sequential decline of -1.4% QoQ, signaling continued subdued discretionary demand

items.target: Gradual recovery expected, no specific numeric target given
items.notes: CFO Aparna Iyer stated margin fell to ~16% (15-quarter low) in Q1 FY2027 on wage hikes and pre-growth investment; recovery expected to take 'several quarters', implying no near-term snapback

items.target: No explicit forward number; momentum highlighted
items.notes: FY2026 large-deal TCV $7.8B (+45.4% YoY); Q1 FY2027 large-deal bookings $1.63B (+12.9% QoQ); management points to bookings strength as the leading indicator for future revenue even as near-term growth stays soft
Interim dividend of ₹11/share declared in FY2026 treated as the final dividend for the year

guidance.management_commentary: CEO Srini Pallia: 'Advancements in AI are reshaping client priorities and creating new opportunities for us to partner more deeply to deliver value-driven outcomes,' and the company is 'pivoting to a services-as-a-software model' via the new AI Native Business & Platforms unit; separately acknowledged the broader demand environment 'remains challenging, with weak discretionary spending and delayed contract execution,' though expects BFSI improvement in Q2 FY2027 and highlighted momentum in technology and communications. CFO Aparna Iyer: organization 'continued to invest in clients, capabilities and people and maintained margins in [a] narrow band' for FY2026, but flagged that Q1 FY2027 margin compression from wage hikes and pre-growth investment will take 'several quarters' to recover, and noted cash conversion remains strong (operating cash flow 112.6% of net income in FY2026).

bull_case: Large-deal bookings are accelerating sharply (FY2026 +45.4% YoY to $7.8B) even as organic revenue stays flat, suggesting a lagged re-acceleration in reported revenue as these deals ramp

New CEO Srini Pallia's consulting-led, AI-powered repositioning (AI Native Business & Platforms unit, Microsoft Copilot partnership, $1B AI investment with 200,000+ staff trained) could allow Wipro to capture AI-native deal flow rather than only being disrupted by it

Disciplined, large-scale capital returns (₹150B/FY2026 buyback at ₹250/share plus steady dividends) support EPS and signal management/promoter (Azim Premji, ~21% stake) confidence despite depressed sentiment (analyst consensus near 'Sell')

Bolt-on M&A (Capco, Rizing, now Mindsprint/Olam) is building vertical consulting depth and anchoring long-duration, high-committed-spend contracts (e.g., Olam's $800M/8-year commitment) that add revenue visibility

Valuation and sentiment are already deeply depressed (stock near 52-week lows around $1.76-1.80, analyst consensus 'Sell' with average target below current price), which limits incremental bad news already being priced in and raises the bar for further downside
bear_case: AI-assisted coding is structurally compressing the economics of Wipro's core commoditized application development/maintenance business (~25% estimated coding-cost reduction), threatening both deal pricing and the labor-arbitrage moat shared with all Indian IT peers

Revenue growth has stalled (FY2026 IT services revenue -0.3% YoY in USD; Q1 FY2027 -1.4% QoQ) and Q2 FY2027 guidance of -1.5% to +0.5% sequential signals no near-term inflection, with discretionary client spending still weak and contract execution delayed

Margins just hit a 15-quarter low (~16% IT services operating margin) on wage inflation and pre-growth investment, with CFO guidance implying several more quarters before recovery — a double hit of slow growth and compressing margins

Wipro has consistently underperformed TCS and Infosys on growth and margin for years, and independent analysts (TBR) expect this gap to persist despite the current AI/consulting pivot, raising execution-risk questions under yet another CEO/strategy reset

Heavy reliance on BFSI (34% of revenue) and discretionary technology/consulting spend makes Wipro acutely exposed to any further global growth slowdown or rate-driven corporate capex pullback, compounded by ongoing INR/USD currency translation volatility
